- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3% above peak or align with 10-day moving average.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.6) and price is rising, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to avoid overbought bias.
- In low-sentiment, low-price regimes (e.g., <70), model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for hidden demand or policy support.
- Model tends to lag in early horizon (1–3 days) when sentiment is volatile; adjust forecast to match 5-day moving average for first 3 days.
- When sentiment drops sharply after a peak, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; apply 1–2% downward correction in next 3–5 days.
- In high-sentiment, high-price regimes, model often overestimates; apply 1–2% downward correction to avoid overvaluation.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.6) and price is flat, model often predicts minor moves; add 0.5–1% upward bias to avoid underestimating volatility.
